prompt: An occupied office is near a busy roadway. Which particle measure most directly represents fine combustion particles that can penetrate deeply into the lungs?

options.text: PM2.5
Carbon dioxide
PM10
Total dissolved solids

explanation: PM2.5 refers to particles with an aerodynamic diameter of 2.5 micrometres or less. These fine particles are commonly produced by combustion and are a key indoor-air-health concern because they can reach deep into the respiratory tract.

distractorExplanations.b: Carbon dioxide is a gas often used as a ventilation indicator, not particulate matter.
distractorExplanations.c: PM10 includes larger inhalable particles and is not the specific fine-particle fraction in the question.
distractorExplanations.d: Total dissolved solids is a water-quality indicator, not an airborne particle metric.

prompt: A facilities manager wants to reduce outdoor smoke and dust entering an air-handling unit. Which filter rating is generally more effective for capturing smaller particles than MERV 8?

options.text: MERV 4
A UV lamp without filtration
A carbon prefilter
MERV 13

explanation: MERV 13 filtration is substantially more effective than MERV 8 at removing smaller airborne particles, including a meaningful portion of fine particulate matter. It is commonly used in higher-performance indoor-air strategies when the system can accommodate the pressure drop.

distractorExplanations.a: MERV 4 is a lower-efficiency filter intended largely for coarse dust and equipment protection.
distractorExplanations.b: UV systems target some microorganisms under controlled conditions but do not physically remove particles.
distractorExplanations.c: Carbon can adsorb some gases but is not a substitute for particle filtration.

prompt: During an indoor air investigation, a project team finds elevated formaldehyde after new composite wood furniture is installed. What is the most appropriate source-control response?

options.text: Keep the furniture and schedule a two-week flush-out before move-in instead of reviewing product emissions
Raise space temperature during occupied hours so the furniture off-gasses its formaldehyde faster
Select furniture verified for low formaldehyde emissions and increase ventilation during the transition
Upgrade the air-handler filters to MERV 13 so the formaldehyde is captured at the return grilles

explanation: The strongest response is to remove or reduce the source by selecting low-emitting products, while using ventilation to dilute remaining emissions. Fragrance and lower filtration do not address formaldehyde emissions.

distractorExplanations.a: A flush-out dilutes formaldehyde temporarily but leaves the emitting furniture in place; it is not source control.
distractorExplanations.b: Heating occupied space speeds emissions while people are present, increasing exposure instead of controlling the source.
distractorExplanations.d: MERV filters capture particles, not gases such as formaldehyde, so a filter upgrade does not address the emitting source.

prompt: Why is carbon dioxide monitoring often used in densely occupied meeting rooms under WELL-aligned operations?

options.text: It gives a direct reading of formaldehyde and other VOCs released by furniture and finishes in the room
It can indicate whether outdoor-air ventilation is keeping pace with occupant-generated contaminants
It confirms that supply air has passed through MERV 13 filtration before it reaches the meeting room
It detects incomplete combustion from nearby equipment before carbon monoxide reaches unsafe levels

explanation: People exhale carbon dioxide, so an elevated indoor level relative to outdoors can signal that ventilation is inadequate for occupancy. It is a ventilation proxy, not a comprehensive pollutant or infection-risk measurement.

distractorExplanations.a: CO2 sensors do not measure VOCs or formaldehyde; CO2 is only a proxy for occupant-related ventilation adequacy.
distractorExplanations.c: Confuses ventilation with filtration: CO2 levels say nothing about filter efficiency, since filters do not remove CO2.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses carbon dioxide with carbon monoxide; combustion hazards require dedicated CO monitoring, not CO2 sensors.

prompt: A tenant wants a smoking policy that best protects nonsmokers in a WELL project. Which policy is most effective?

options.text: Prohibit smoking and vaping inside and locate any permitted outdoor smoking well away from entries, operable windows and air intakes
Allow smoking in a dedicated conference room with the door closed
Allow smoking near the main entrance after business hours
Use scented air fresheners in indoor smoking areas

explanation: Eliminating indoor smoking and keeping outdoor smoke sources away from openings and air intakes reduces secondhand-smoke exposure and contaminant migration into the building.

distractorExplanations.b: Closing a door does not reliably prevent tobacco smoke from migrating through gaps or shared HVAC systems.
distractorExplanations.c: Smoke at entrances exposes arriving occupants and can be drawn indoors.
distractorExplanations.d: Air fresheners do not remove smoke constituents and may introduce additional irritants.

prompt: A building experiences a two-week period of wildfire smoke. Which temporary operations package best reduces indoor particle exposure?

options.text: Switch the air handlers to full economizer mode so stale indoor air is diluted with outdoor air more quickly
Run ozone-generating air purifiers on each occupied floor to neutralize smoke particles and lingering odours
Seal obvious envelope leaks, use appropriately rated particle filtration, and reduce outdoor-air intake only as allowed
Keep the standard MERV 8 filters in place and open operable windows to equalize indoor and outdoor pressure during the event

explanation: During smoke events, a controlled approach combines filtration, envelope management and carefully adjusted ventilation consistent with health and code requirements. The goal is to limit particle ingress without creating unacceptable indoor-air conditions. Essential ventilation must still be maintained while outdoor-air intake is reduced.

distractorExplanations.a: Full economizer mode pulls in more smoke-laden outdoor air during a wildfire event, raising indoor PM2.5 instead of lowering it.
distractorExplanations.b: Ozone generators do not remove particles and add a respiratory irritant that reacts with indoor chemicals to form new pollutants.
distractorExplanations.d: MERV 8 captures few fine smoke particles, and opening windows admits smoke directly, so indoor exposure would rise.

prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from particulate matter?

options.text: VOCs are particles smaller than 2.5 micrometres, whereas particulate matter refers to gases released by combustion
VOCs are inorganic gases such as ozone and carbon monoxide, whereas particulate matter consists of organic vapours
VOCs are gases emitted from sources such as paints and cleaners, whereas particulate matter consists of suspended solid or liquid particles
VOCs are tracked with CO2 sensors as a ventilation proxy, whereas particulate matter is assessed by culturing airborne mould spores in a laboratory

explanation: VOCs are carbon-containing chemicals that can off-gas as gases from many products and activities. Particulate matter is a mixture of airborne particles and droplets with different sources, behaviour and control methods.

distractorExplanations.a: Swaps the two definitions: PM2.5 describes particle size, while VOCs are gaseous organic compounds, not particles.
distractorExplanations.b: VOCs are organic compounds; ozone and CO are inorganic gases, and particulate matter is particles, not vapours.
distractorExplanations.d: CO2 sensors do not measure VOCs, and PM is measured by particle counters or gravimetric methods, not microbial culture.

prompt: An office introduces a new fragrance-diffusion system to improve perceived cleanliness. Which WELL-aligned concern should the project team raise first?

options.text: The system will necessarily increase drinking-water lead levels
The system can add VOCs and sensitizers without correcting the underlying source of odors
The system will improve MERV efficiency by coating filters
The system eliminates the need for a cleaning protocol

explanation: Fragrances can contribute chemical emissions and trigger sensitivities. A healthier approach identifies odor sources, improves cleaning or ventilation as appropriate, and avoids masking contamination.

distractorExplanations.a: Fragrance diffusion is unrelated to lead in potable water.
distractorExplanations.c: A fragrance device does not improve a filter's particle-capture efficiency.
distractorExplanations.d: Scent is not a substitute for routine, effective cleaning.

prompt: A mechanical engineer proposes installing bipolar ionization in an occupied office. What is the most prudent WELL-oriented evaluation step before relying on it?

options.text: Accept the manufacturer's laboratory claims and reduce outdoor-air ventilation in proportion to its stated clean-air rate
Confirm the device carries an electrical safety listing and treat that listing as proof of pathogen and particle removal
Run it in place of MERV 13 filtration, since ionization makes particles settle out of the breathing zone onto surfaces
Review independent evidence for effectiveness and verify that the device does not generate harmful ozone or by-products

explanation: Emerging air-cleaning technologies should be assessed for verified performance and unintended chemical by-products, particularly ozone. They complement rather than automatically replace source control, ventilation and filtration. That verification should reflect installed operating conditions, not only laboratory claims.

distractorExplanations.a: Relying on vendor claims and cutting outdoor air removes a proven control before the device's real-world benefit is shown.
distractorExplanations.b: An electrical safety listing addresses shock and fire risk; it does not demonstrate air-cleaning effectiveness or by-products.
distractorExplanations.c: Ionization is not a substitute for rated filtration; particles deposited on surfaces can be resuspended and are not removed.

prompt: Which indoor relative-humidity range is generally targeted to limit both excessive dryness and moisture conditions that support mould growth?

options.text: Approximately 5% to 15%
Approximately 15% to 25%
Approximately 30% to 60%
Approximately 65% to 85%

explanation: Maintaining indoor relative humidity roughly between 30% and 60% supports comfort and reduces conditions associated with overly dry mucous membranes or dampness, condensation and biological growth.

distractorExplanations.a: This range is far too dry; it causes eye, skin and mucous-membrane irritation and static discomfort for occupants.
distractorExplanations.b: Still below the commonly targeted 30% lower bound, so dryness complaints and irritation remain likely in winter.
distractorExplanations.d: Humidity above about 60% supports mould growth and dust mites, which is exactly what the target range is meant to avoid.

prompt: A ceiling stain appears below a chilled-water pipe. What action should occur first to protect indoor air quality?

options.text: Treat the stain with a biocide and repaint with mould-resistant paint, then schedule the pipe repair for the next shutdown
Collect air samples for mould spores first and wait for laboratory results before deciding whether to repair the pipe
Stop the moisture source, dry affected materials promptly, and assess whether porous materials need removal or remediation
Increase supply airflow so the wet ceiling tile dries in place, and replace the pipe insulation at the next scheduled PM

explanation: Moisture control is fundamental to preventing mould. The leak must be corrected and materials dried or remediated promptly; filtration alone cannot fix moisture-damaged building materials.

distractorExplanations.a: Cosmetic treatment before stopping the leak leaves wet materials in place and allows microbial growth to continue.
distractorExplanations.b: Sampling is secondary; the first step is to stop the moisture source and dry materials, since mould can grow within 24-48 hours.
distractorExplanations.d: Drying in place without fixing the condensation source lets the tile re-wet, and porous materials may already need removal.

prompt: A project team suspects elevated radon in a ground-floor childcare space. Which approach is appropriate?

options.text: Install a carbon monoxide detector in the room, since the same sensor also alarms when radon levels are elevated
Test the drinking water for radon and treat the indoor air only if the water result exceeds the limit
Increase recirculation through MERV 13 filters, which capture radon gas before it reaches the breathing zone
Conduct radon testing using an accepted method and implement mitigation if results are elevated

explanation: Radon is a radioactive soil gas that cannot be seen or smelled. Testing is required to identify elevated levels, and mitigation commonly reduces soil-gas entry or depressurizes beneath the slab.

distractorExplanations.a: CO detectors do not detect radon; radon requires dedicated short- or long-term radon testing with an accepted method.
distractorExplanations.b: Soil gas entering through the slab is the main radon pathway, so a water test cannot rule out an indoor-air problem.
distractorExplanations.c: Radon is a gas that passes through particle filters; mitigation relies on testing and measures such as sub-slab depressurization.

prompt: Which situation most strongly warrants carbon monoxide monitoring in a building?

options.text: An occupied office with high CO2 readings during back-to-back meetings
An occupied area adjacent to fuel-burning equipment or an enclosed parking garage
A laboratory using electric hot plates and sealed reagent storage cabinets
A newly carpeted open office with elevated total VOC readings after the installation

explanation: Carbon monoxide is produced by incomplete combustion and may accumulate near combustion appliances, vehicle exhaust or attached garages. Monitoring and proper exhaust are important safeguards in such settings.

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses carbon dioxide with carbon monoxide; high CO2 signals under-ventilation, not a combustion source that needs CO monitoring.
distractorExplanations.c: Electric heating produces no combustion by-products, so it is not a CO source; chemical storage calls for other controls.
distractorExplanations.d: Elevated TVOCs call for VOC source control and flush-out; carpet emissions do not produce carbon monoxide.

prompt: A cooking classroom has strong odours and ultrafine particles during frying demonstrations. Which design measure most directly captures contaminants at their source?

options.text: A recirculating range hood with a charcoal filter returning air to the room
A higher room air-change rate from the general HVAC supply diffusers
A properly designed and commissioned local exhaust hood vented outdoors
A portable HEPA air cleaner placed in the far corner of the classroom

explanation: Local exhaust hoods capture cooking pollutants, heat and moisture before they disperse into the room. They are more effective source control than dilution, fragrances or air mixing alone.

distractorExplanations.a: A recirculating charcoal hood returns ultrafine particles and moisture to the room instead of exhausting them outdoors.
distractorExplanations.b: General dilution ventilation spreads contaminants through the room first; it does not capture them at the cooktop source.
distractorExplanations.d: A distant room air cleaner treats air after contaminants have spread; it is not local capture at the frying source.

prompt: Why should a WELL project maintain an HVAC filter replacement log?

options.text: To document the MERV rating needed for ventilation credit, since a filter log replaces outdoor-air verification
To verify that filtration performance is maintained and replacements occur before excessive loading compromises airflow
To track filter costs so replacement can be deferred until occupants report visible dust from the diffusers
To show that filters were changed once at construction completion, which satisfies the ongoing operations requirement for WELL

explanation: A documented maintenance schedule helps ensure filters remain installed correctly and are changed when needed. Neglected filters can increase pressure drop, reduce delivered airflow and permit contaminant bypass if damaged or poorly seated. Overloaded or poorly seated filters also compromise bypass control.

distractorExplanations.a: Filtration and outdoor-air delivery are separate requirements; a filter log does not verify ventilation rates.
distractorExplanations.c: Waiting for visible dust means filters are already overloaded or bypassing; replacement should follow a planned schedule.
distractorExplanations.d: A single change at handover does not demonstrate ongoing maintenance; the log exists to track recurring replacements.

prompt: An air sample shows high total VOC concentrations after a weekend carpet installation. Which sequence best reflects a source-control hierarchy?

options.text: Use low-emitting products first, isolate or schedule high-emitting work, then ventilate and flush out the space before occupancy
Ventilate and flush out the space first, then switch to low-emitting products on the next installation if TVOCs persist
Install portable air cleaners with HEPA filters and retest TVOCs, since particle filtration removes VOC emissions
Raise space temperature during occupied hours to accelerate off-gassing, then reduce ventilation once odours fade

explanation: Source reduction is preferred, followed by exposure management during installation and adequate ventilation before occupants return. This hierarchy addresses actual emissions instead of merely concealing their presence.

distractorExplanations.b: Reverses the hierarchy: source control through low-emitting products comes first, with ventilation and flush-out after.
distractorExplanations.c: HEPA filters capture particles, not gaseous VOCs, so this neither controls the source nor removes the measured TVOCs.
distractorExplanations.d: Heating during occupancy raises exposure, and cutting ventilation based on odour ignores measured TVOC levels.

prompt: For a drinking-water testing plan, why should samples be collected after water has remained in plumbing for a defined stagnation period when assessing lead risk?

options.text: Stagnation flushes sediment out of the service line, giving a cleaner baseline sample for comparison
Stagnation can reveal metals that leach from plumbing components into standing water
Stagnation lets the chlorine residual rise, which the laboratory needs before lead can be measured
Stagnation samples measure the lead level supplied by the utility at the water main before the building

explanation: First-draw or stagnation sampling is designed to characterize water that has been in contact with pipes, fittings and fixtures, where lead or other metals may leach. Sampling protocols must be followed consistently for interpretable results.

distractorExplanations.a: Stagnation does the opposite: standing water picks up metals from plumbing; flushed samples, not stagnant ones, give a baseline.
distractorExplanations.c: Chlorine residual decays during stagnation, and lead analysis does not depend on residual disinfectant levels.
distractorExplanations.d: First-draw stagnant samples reflect the building's own fixtures and pipes, not the utility supply at the main.

prompt: A school has an elevated lead result at one drinking fountain. What is the most appropriate immediate response?

options.text: Remove the fixture from service, provide safe alternative drinking water, investigate the source and remediate
Flush the fountain for two minutes each morning and keep it in use while a follow-up sample is scheduled
Install a carbon filter certified only for taste and odour, then return the fountain to use without any retesting
Post a notice asking pupils to run the water briefly and continue use until the annual sampling round

explanation: Potentially contaminated fixtures should be taken out of service while the source is identified and corrected. Safe alternative access prevents an interruption in hydration while remediation and follow-up testing occur. The fixture returns to use only after remediation and confirmatory testing.

distractorExplanations.b: Daily flushing is a temporary measure that does not make an elevated-lead fixture safe for continued pupil use.
distractorExplanations.c: A taste-and-odour certification does not cover lead reduction, and returning it without retesting leaves the risk unverified.
distractorExplanations.d: Relying on pupils to flush and waiting for the next annual round leaves children exposed to a known lead result.

prompt: Which strategy most directly supports equitable drinking-water access in a large workplace?

options.text: Provide subsidized bottled water at a central cafeteria that is open during the standard lunch hours on each weekday
Install one drinking fountain per floor beside the restrooms, without considering travel distance from desks
Provide free water stations in staff break rooms that are accessible to badge holders of a single department
Provide free, clearly marked potable-water stations within convenient travel distance of all regularly occupied areas

explanation: Convenient, free and visible potable-water access reduces barriers to hydration for all occupants. Stations should be maintained and located where people work, learn or exercise.

distractorExplanations.a: Paid, centralized water with limited hours creates cost and access barriers rather than free, convenient water.
distractorExplanations.b: A fixed count per floor can leave large areas far from water; equitable access is based on travel distance to occupied areas.
distractorExplanations.c: Limiting access to one department's badge holders excludes other regular occupants, which is not equitable access.

prompt: A building installs bottle-filling stations. Which additional feature most meaningfully supports ongoing trust in water quality?

options.text: A filter-change indicator light on each station, which replaces the need for periodic water-quality testing
A one-time water test at commissioning, displayed as a certificate beside the station for the life of the building
A UV sanitizing lamp in the dispensing nozzle, used in place of a documented maintenance and cleaning schedule
A documented maintenance and testing programme with clear communication of the water source and service status

explanation: Visible access must be paired with reliable operations. Documented maintenance, timely filter changes, testing where applicable and transparent communication support confidence in potable-water quality.

distractorExplanations.a: An indicator light only tracks filter life; it does not verify water quality or communicate the source and service status.
distractorExplanations.b: Water quality can change over time; trust depends on ongoing testing and maintenance, not a single handover result.
distractorExplanations.c: A UV nozzle lamp addresses surface microbes at the outlet but does not replace routine maintenance, testing or communication.

prompt: A hotel has low occupancy for several months and plans to reopen. Which water-management action is most important for controlling Legionella risk?

options.text: Shock-chlorinate the water heater once on reopening day and resume normal occupancy without further flushing
Lower the water heater setpoint during the closure to save energy, then flush the guest-room showers on the day of reopening
Test potable water for lead and copper before reopening, since metals testing also indicates Legionella risk
Follow a documented water management plan, including flushing, temperature control, inspections and corrective actions

explanation: Extended stagnation can create conditions favourable to Legionella. A risk-based water management plan addresses system recommissioning, temperature, disinfectant residuals, flushing and verification before occupants return. These steps should be completed before the hotel reopens to guests.

distractorExplanations.a: A single shock treatment without flushing stagnant branch lines and ongoing control does not manage Legionella risk.
distractorExplanations.b: Lower hot-water temperatures during stagnation create Legionella growth conditions; flushing showers alone does not undo that.
distractorExplanations.c: Lead and copper results say nothing about Legionella; microbial risk needs a water management plan and targeted controls.

prompt: Why are domestic hot-water temperatures and recirculation important in Legionella control?

options.text: They keep hot water near 35 °C, which limits scalding risk and also stops Legionella growth
They remove the need for a water management plan once the circulating loop exceeds 50 °C
They help avoid long periods in temperature ranges that can support Legionella growth
They reduce lead leaching from old solder, which is the main way Legionella enters building water

explanation: Legionella control includes managing temperature throughout hot-water storage and distribution so water does not stagnate in a favourable growth range. Scald protection is handled separately at points of use. Delivery temperatures must still be managed to avoid scalding at outlets.

distractorExplanations.a: Around 35 °C is close to the ideal Legionella growth range; control relies on keeping water outside roughly 20-50 °C.
distractorExplanations.b: Temperature control is one element of a water management plan; it does not replace monitoring, flushing and corrective actions.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses metals leaching with microbial risk; Legionella growth relates to temperature, stagnation and biofilm, not solder.

prompt: A project is selecting a point-of-use water filter for a known contaminant. What should the team verify rather than relying on a generic 'purified water' claim?

options.text: Certification that the filter meets taste and odour reduction claims, which also covers lead and microbial health contaminants
A manufacturer's in-house test report showing high contaminant removal at a flow rate above the rated capacity
Third-party certification that the specific filter reduces the target contaminant under its intended operating conditions
A filter with the smallest micron rating available, since pore size alone determines which chemicals are removed

explanation: Filtration must be matched to the contaminant of concern and supported by credible performance certification. A vague marketing claim does not show that a device reduces lead, cysts, chemicals or other specific contaminants.

distractorExplanations.a: Taste-and-odour (aesthetic) certification does not verify reduction of health contaminants such as lead or microbes.
distractorExplanations.b: An in-house report is not independent certification, and results above rated flow do not reflect intended operating conditions.
distractorExplanations.d: Micron rating describes particle capture; dissolved chemicals are removed by specific media, verified by contaminant-specific certification.

prompt: What is the principal purpose of a backflow prevention device at a potable-water connection?

options.text: To prevent contaminated water from flowing backward into the drinking-water supply
To reduce excess pressure in the potable system so pipes and fixtures are not damaged
To keep hot water from cooling in the riser and creating Legionella growth conditions
To remove lead and copper particles before water reaches drinking fountains and taps

explanation: Backflow prevention protects potable water by stopping reverse flow from irrigation, process equipment or other non-potable systems when pressure conditions change.

distractorExplanations.b: Confuses a backflow preventer with a pressure-reducing valve, which limits supply pressure rather than preventing reverse flow.
distractorExplanations.c: Describes the purpose of hot-water recirculation, not a backflow device, which stops contaminated water reversing into potable lines.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses backflow prevention with point-of-use filtration; a backflow device does not treat or filter water.

prompt: In a WELL project, which practice best reduces the risk that cleaning products contaminate drinking-water fixtures?

options.text: Switch to stronger concentrated disinfectants so fountains can be cleaned less often between sampling rounds
Fill chemical dilution buckets at drinking fountains, which have better water quality than janitor's sinks
Rely on fountain bottle-filler filters to remove any cleaning-chemical residue left on the outlet surface after each cleaning
Train staff to use approved products and procedures and avoid storing or mixing chemicals near potable-water outlets

explanation: Clear storage, handling and cleaning procedures prevent accidental chemical contamination while still maintaining hygienic fixtures. Drinking-water systems should be protected from improper chemical use.

distractorExplanations.a: Stronger concentrates raise residue and exposure risk at outlets; the control is approved products, procedures and storage.
distractorExplanations.b: Filling or mixing chemicals at drinking outlets is precisely how cross-contamination occurs; use designated service sinks.
distractorExplanations.c: Filters treat water inside the unit, not chemical residue on the outlet surface, so they do not prevent contamination.

prompt: A food-service operator asks how to align its menu with WELL Nourishment. Which change is most directly aligned?

options.text: Add calorie counts to the menu board while keeping fried entrées as the featured default option at each station
Make fruits, vegetables and minimally processed options prominent, appealing and readily available
Replace sugar-sweetened beverages with diet soft drinks and keep the rest of the menu unchanged
Offer a weekly salad special while keeping desserts and chips at every checkout point

explanation: WELL Nourishment encourages environments that make healthier choices easy and attractive, including access to fruit, vegetables and nutritious meal options rather than relying only on individual willpower.

distractorExplanations.a: Labelling alone leaves the less healthy option as the default; Nourishment emphasizes making healthier foods prominent.
distractorExplanations.c: Swapping to diet drinks does not increase fruits, vegetables or minimally processed foods, which is the core menu shift.
distractorExplanations.d: An occasional special does not make healthy options readily available, and checkout confectionery keeps the unhealthy default.

prompt: Which cafeteria merchandising tactic most effectively nudges healthier choices without banning other foods?

options.text: Place a calorie-count poster at the exit while keeping the current product placement unchanged
Stop selling sugary drinks and stock only water and unsweetened tea instead
Place fruit, vegetables and water at eye level and at the start of the service line
Discount healthier items at the end of the line after trays are already filled

explanation: Prominent placement and convenient availability are evidence-informed choice-architecture strategies. They make nutritious options easier to notice and select while preserving choice.

distractorExplanations.a: Information shown after choices are made does not nudge selection; placement at the point of choice does.
distractorExplanations.b: Removing products is a ban, which the question excludes; nudging changes placement and prominence, not availability.
distractorExplanations.d: Placing healthier items after trays are full reduces their influence; nudges work at eye level and the start of the line.

prompt: A workplace wants to improve nutritional transparency for prepared meals. Which practice is most useful?

options.text: Provide clear nutrition and allergen information for standard menu items in a format employees can access before choosing
Post nutrition and allergen details on the company intranet once a year, even though the menu rotates every week
Display calorie counts at the register for standard items and give allergen details to diners only on request
Print detailed ingredient and allergen lists on receipts so employees can review the information after each purchase

explanation: Accessible nutrition and allergen information supports informed selection and reduces risk for people with food allergies or dietary needs. Information should be legible and available at the decision point.

distractorExplanations.b: Annually updated information goes out of date when menus rotate, so employees cannot rely on it when choosing meals.
distractorExplanations.c: Calories at the register come too late, and allergen details held by staff are not accessible to employees before choosing.
distractorExplanations.d: Receipt information arrives after the purchase, which defeats transparency meant to inform the choice beforehand.

prompt: Which procurement approach best supports healthier food availability in a corporate pantry?

options.text: Stock products chosen by employee vote each month, with no nutrition criteria applied to the final shortlist
Buy reduced-fat versions of current snacks, even where those versions contain more added sugar
Set purchasing standards that prioritise nutritious snacks and beverages while limiting high-sugar options
Offer free sugar-sweetened drinks as a staff perk while placing fruit in a paid vending machine

explanation: Procurement standards influence the default food environment. Prioritising nutritious offerings and limiting routine access to high-sugar products supports health without eliminating all individual choice. The aim is to limit routine availability of high-sugar items rather than ban them outright.

distractorExplanations.a: Preference voting without nutrition criteria does not ensure healthier availability; procurement standards are needed.
distractorExplanations.b: Reduced-fat products often add sugar, so this can worsen the high-sugar profile the policy is meant to limit.
distractorExplanations.d: Making sugary drinks free and fruit paid creates the opposite price incentive from healthier food availability.

prompt: A project is reviewing food advertising in a school cafeteria. Which approach best reflects WELL Nourishment principles?

options.text: Allow branded energy-drink displays beside the water station if the vendor also funds a nutrition education poster nearby
Keep existing soda advertising but add calorie labels to the advertised products
Restrict marketing of highly processed, high-sugar foods while using the space to promote healthier options
Restrict advertising only during lunch periods while allowing sugary-drink ads at other times

explanation: The food environment includes messaging as well as availability. Limiting promotion of less healthy products and positively highlighting nutritious choices reduces conflicting cues, especially in settings serving children.

distractorExplanations.a: Sponsorship of a poster does not offset marketing of high-sugar products, which WELL Nourishment seeks to restrict.
distractorExplanations.b: Labels do not remove promotional pressure; the principle is to restrict marketing of high-sugar, highly processed foods.
distractorExplanations.d: Students see ads throughout the day; time-limited restriction still markets high-sugar products in the cafeteria.

prompt: Why is a dedicated, hygienic lactation room relevant to the WELL v2 Community concept (C09 New Mother Support)?

options.text: It satisfies the potable-water feature because the room includes a sink supplied with tested drinking water
It counts as a restorative space under Mind, so it can double as the building's quiet room
It provides a dedicated food-preparation area where infant formula is sold to employees
It supports breastfeeding and allows nursing parents to express and store milk safely and privately

explanation: WELL v2 places lactation support in the Community concept (C09 New Mother Support): a private, hygienic, non-restroom room with seating, power and milk storage lets nursing parents breastfeed or express milk at work.

distractorExplanations.a: A sink may be an amenity in the room, but the room's purpose is breastfeeding support, not meeting drinking-water features.
distractorExplanations.b: Sharing the room as a general quiet room undermines the privacy and availability that nursing parents need.
distractorExplanations.c: A lactation room supports expressing and storing breast milk; it is not a retail or food-preparation space.

prompt: A campus is planning a community garden. Which feature most directly makes it a credible nourishment intervention rather than a decorative landscape?

options.text: Raised planters of ornamental grasses with signage about local plant species
A programme for growing edible produce with safe soil and water practices
Edible plants grown in reclaimed soil without testing, open to anyone at any time
A vegetable plot maintained by contractors whose harvest is sold off site

explanation: A nourishment garden should support safe cultivation, learning or access to edible food. Soil safety, irrigation quality, integrated pest management and participant guidance are important implementation details. Access rules and education or use by occupants complete a credible garden programme.

distractorExplanations.a: Ornamental planting with signage is landscape and biophilia, not food production, so it is not a nourishment intervention.
distractorExplanations.c: Untested soil can carry lead or other contaminants, so produce grown this way lacks the safe soil practices required.
distractorExplanations.d: If occupants neither use the produce nor engage with the garden, it does not function as an occupant nourishment strategy.

prompt: Which integrated pest management (IPM) action should be taken before routine pesticide application in a food-preparation area?

options.text: Identify the pest and eliminate food, water, entry and harborage conditions through sanitation and exclusion
Apply a broad-spectrum pesticide on a fixed monthly schedule as a preventive barrier in each prep area
Set bait stations first and review sanitation only if pest sightings continue after three months
Fog the kitchen after hours with a residual insecticide, then wipe the food-contact surfaces before opening the next day

explanation: IPM prioritises prevention, monitoring and least-toxic controls. Correcting sanitation, moisture and entry pathways often addresses the underlying cause and reduces reliance on pesticide exposure.

distractorExplanations.b: Calendar-based spraying is the opposite of IPM, which applies pesticides only after identification and non-chemical controls.
distractorExplanations.c: IPM starts with identification, sanitation and exclusion; baiting first and delaying sanitation reverses that order.
distractorExplanations.d: Fogging is a high-exposure chemical step that IPM reserves for last, after the conditions supporting pests are removed.

prompt: A cleaning contractor plans to use aerosol disinfectant sprays daily in an occupied open office. What is the best WELL-aligned modification?

options.text: Switch to a stronger quaternary ammonium spray applied less often, keeping the aerosol method unchanged
Keep daily aerosol spraying but schedule it at noon, when outdoor-air ventilation rates are at their peak
Replace disinfection with fragrance-free air fresheners, since odour control is the main WELL cleaning goal
Use a risk-based cleaning protocol with lower-emitting products and targeted application methods

explanation: Effective hygiene does not require indiscriminate aerosolisation. Targeted, documented cleaning with safer products and appropriate ventilation reduces unnecessary respiratory exposure while preserving sanitation. Required disinfection is still performed where the risk warrants it.

distractorExplanations.a: Stronger quats sprayed as aerosols still create inhalation exposure; the fix is lower-emitting products and targeted application.
distractorExplanations.b: Spraying at noon exposes occupants during peak occupancy; higher ventilation does not remove the aerosol source.
distractorExplanations.c: Air fresheners add emissions and do not disinfect; WELL cleaning aims to reduce exposure while keeping necessary disinfection.

prompt: What is the primary indoor-air concern with an ozone-generating air cleaner used in occupied rooms?

options.text: Ozone can irritate the respiratory system and react with indoor chemicals to form additional pollutants
Ozone breaks down quickly into oxygen, so its main concern is reduced filter life in the AHU
Ozone raises indoor CO2 levels, which forces the ventilation system to bring in more outdoor air to compensate
Ozone removes VOCs effectively, but it can bleach fabrics and finishes after prolonged exposure

explanation: Ozone is a reactive respiratory irritant. In occupied environments, ozone generators can create direct exposure and secondary pollutants, so they are not an appropriate general-purpose air-cleaning solution.

distractorExplanations.b: Ozone persists long enough indoors to harm occupants; the primary concern is respiratory irritation, not filter life.
distractorExplanations.c: Ozone does not produce CO2; its concerns are respiratory irritation and reactions forming secondary pollutants.
distractorExplanations.d: Ozone reacts with VOCs to create new pollutants such as formaldehyde rather than removing them, and harms people first.

prompt: A WELL project uses portable air cleaners in a renovated suite. Which selection criterion is most important for particle control?

options.text: A UV-C lamp inside the unit, since ultraviolet light removes particles from the airstream
A clean air delivery rate appropriate for the room size, with no harmful ozone production
The highest fan airflow in cubic feet per minute, even with a low-efficiency mesh filter
An ionizer setting that charges particles so they settle on nearby room surfaces

explanation: Portable cleaners should be sized by their clean air delivery capacity for the intended room and should not produce harmful by-products. They can supplement, but not replace, source control and ventilation.

distractorExplanations.a: UV-C can inactivate microbes but does not capture particles; particle control depends on filtration and CADR.
distractorExplanations.c: Raw airflow is not clean air delivery; CADR combines airflow with filter efficiency, so a mesh filter yields little.
distractorExplanations.d: Settled particles are not removed and can be resuspended, and ionizers may emit ozone, which the key excludes.

prompt: After a dust-generating renovation, what verification method most directly demonstrates that the occupied area has been cleaned before reoccupation?

options.text: Run the HVAC on full recirculation for 24 hours, then reoccupy once visible dust is no longer present
Replace the air-handler filters after reoccupation, since filter loading is the best sign that dust has been removed
Conduct documented post-construction cleaning and, where required, verify airborne contaminants through appropriate testing
Rely on the contractor's verbal confirmation of cleaning and measure CO2 levels on the first day of occupancy

explanation: Post-construction air quality depends on physical cleaning, HVAC protection and, when appropriate, testing against relevant parameters. Odor, lighting and food service do not demonstrate removal of construction contaminants.

distractorExplanations.a: Recirculation spreads construction dust, and visual checks cannot confirm fine particles have been cleaned or removed.
distractorExplanations.b: Changing filters after people return does not verify the space is clean; documented cleaning and testing come before reoccupation.
distractorExplanations.d: Verbal assurance is not documentation, and CO2 indicates ventilation rather than construction dust or airborne contaminants.

prompt: Which condition is most likely to cause moisture-related microbial growth inside a building envelope?

options.text: Indoor relative humidity held near 35% during winter, with continuous exhaust running in the bathrooms and kitchens
A vapour-open wall assembly that lets small amounts of moisture dry toward the exterior
Persistent condensation on cold surfaces due to uncontrolled humid indoor air and thermal bridges
Short-term high humidity during a summer storm in a building with an intact air barrier

explanation: Condensation provides sustained moisture on materials and can enable mould growth, especially where thermal bridging creates cold surfaces. Moisture control requires envelope, ventilation and humidity management.

distractorExplanations.a: Moderate winter humidity with wet-room exhaust is a moisture control measure, not a cause of envelope microbial growth.
distractorExplanations.b: Vapour-open assemblies allow drying, which reduces rather than causes moisture accumulation in the envelope.
distractorExplanations.d: Brief humidity spikes with an intact air barrier rarely cause growth; persistent condensation on cold surfaces does.

prompt: A building has a cooling tower. Why does its water management matter to occupant health?

options.text: Cooling-tower drift releases lead particles that settle in nearby drinking-water outlets
Cooling towers raise indoor CO2 when their plume is drawn back into outdoor-air intakes
Poorly controlled cooling towers can amplify and disseminate Legionella-containing aerosols
Cooling-tower water mixes with the domestic hot-water loop, which spreads Legionella to taps

explanation: Cooling towers can generate aerosols, so poorly maintained systems are a recognized Legionella risk. A water management programme addresses treatment, monitoring, cleaning and corrective action.

distractorExplanations.a: Cooling-tower health risk is Legionella in drift aerosols; towers are not a lead source for drinking-water outlets.
distractorExplanations.b: Plume re-entrainment matters because of Legionella aerosols, not CO2; cooling-tower water does not generate CO2.
distractorExplanations.d: Condenser water and domestic water are separate systems; the tower risk is aerosol dissemination of Legionella.

prompt: What is the best reason to place a water bottle-filling station near an active stairwell or fitness area?

options.text: It makes hydration convenient at a point where people may be physically active or passing through regularly
It allows the project to omit drinking water on upper floors because the stairwell station serves the building
It helps meet the Thermal Comfort concept by cooling occupants who use the stairs during summer
It replaces separate drinking-fountain maintenance because fitness staff can test the station weekly

explanation: Conveniently located water stations encourage regular hydration, particularly near activity areas. They complement, rather than replace, accessible potable water throughout the building.

distractorExplanations.b: One well-placed station does not replace convenient water access near the other regularly occupied areas.
distractorExplanations.c: Hydration placement supports Water and Movement goals; it is not a Thermal Comfort strategy for cooling occupants.
distractorExplanations.d: Placement does not change maintenance obligations; every potable outlet still needs documented upkeep and testing.

prompt: A café proposes offering only sugar-sweetened beverages at checkout while keeping water in a back room. What is the strongest WELL Nourishment critique?

options.text: The arrangement is acceptable if calorie labels are posted on each beverage at the checkout cooler
The arrangement mainly breaches food-safety rules because beverages must be stored away from the register
The arrangement is acceptable if the water is free, since price alone determines WELL beverage compliance
The arrangement makes the less healthy default most convenient and creates an unnecessary barrier to water access

explanation: Product placement shapes behavior. Prominent sugary beverages and hidden water make healthier choices harder, contrary to strategies that support hydration and limit routine sugar-sweetened beverage promotion.

distractorExplanations.a: Labels do not fix the problem that the unhealthy option is the convenient default while water is hidden.
distractorExplanations.b: The WELL Nourishment issue is choice architecture and water access, not a food-safety storage rule.
distractorExplanations.c: Free water kept in a back room is still a barrier; visibility and convenience matter alongside price.

prompt: Which meal description is the best example of an inclusive healthier-food offering?

options.text: A vegan meal served in large portions and labelled 'healthy', but with no ingredient or allergen information posted
A low-calorie salad with calorie counts listed, but with no protein option or allergen labelling for diners
A clearly labelled vegetable-forward meal with whole-grain and protein options, including ingredient and allergen information
A gluten-free meal offered on request, with ingredients listed on a sheet that is kept in the kitchen

explanation: A nutritious option should be genuinely available, clearly described and usable by people with dietary needs. Ingredient and allergen transparency supports informed selection alongside balanced meal composition.

distractorExplanations.a: A plant-based label is not enough; without ingredient and allergen information, the meal is not inclusive or transparent.
distractorExplanations.b: Calorie counts alone omit allergen information and balanced protein options, so the offering is neither complete nor inclusive.
distractorExplanations.d: Information held in the kitchen is not accessible at the point of choice, and an on-request meal is not a standard offering.

prompt: A facilities team receives complaints about visible dust from supply diffusers. Which investigation is most appropriate?

options.text: Replace the diffusers with a style that throws air away from desks so the dust is less visible to occupants
Inspect filter fit and replacement history, duct cleanliness and sources of particle generation
Increase the outdoor-air rate, since visible dust from diffusers indicates that CO2 levels in the zone are too high
Schedule duct cleaning across the whole building at once, before checking filters or local dust sources

explanation: Visible dust warrants a systematic review of filtration installation, maintenance, source control and possible construction contamination. The response should identify the particulate source rather than mask it. Construction dust controls should be checked as part of the same investigation.

distractorExplanations.a: Changing diffuser throw hides the symptom; the investigation should find where the particles enter or bypass filtration.
distractorExplanations.c: Visible dust is a particle and filtration problem; it does not indicate elevated CO2 or under-ventilation.
distractorExplanations.d: Building-wide duct cleaning before diagnosis is costly and may not fix a filter bypass or nearby construction source.

prompt: What is the main purpose of commissioning outdoor-air ventilation rates in a new office?

options.text: To confirm the design calculations meet code, which removes the need to measure airflow after installation
To confirm that the installed system delivers the intended outdoor air to occupied zones under operating conditions
To set the filter MERV rating, since outdoor-air rate commissioning is mainly a filtration requirement
To record the outdoor-air damper position at the AHU, which proves the airflow reaching each occupied zone

explanation: Ventilation commissioning verifies that design intent translates into actual airflow, controls and distribution. This is essential because adequate ventilation is a core control for occupant-generated and indoor chemical contaminants.

distractorExplanations.a: Design review is not commissioning; commissioning measures what the installed system actually delivers in operation.
distractorExplanations.c: Confuses filtration with ventilation; outdoor-air commissioning verifies airflow quantity, not filter efficiency.
distractorExplanations.d: Damper position does not prove delivered airflow; zone-level measurement under operating conditions is needed.

prompt: An air-quality dashboard reports a low CO2 level but elevated TVOCs after renovation. What conclusion is most accurate?

options.text: Ventilation for occupancy may be adequate, but source emissions still require investigation and control
Low CO2 shows the TVOC sensor is faulty, since both readings rise and fall together with the number of occupants
TVOC levels will fall on their own once CO2 rises, so no source investigation is required
The outdoor-air rate should be reduced because low CO2 shows the space is over-ventilated

explanation: CO2 is primarily a proxy for occupant-related ventilation adequacy, not a universal indicator of all pollutants. Elevated VOCs can arise from materials or activities despite acceptable CO2 readings.

distractorExplanations.b: TVOCs come largely from materials and products, not people, so they can be high while occupant-driven CO2 is low.
distractorExplanations.c: Rising CO2 means less ventilation per person, which would tend to raise TVOCs; post-renovation sources still need review.
distractorExplanations.d: Cutting ventilation while renovation emissions are elevated would increase TVOC exposure rather than address the source.

prompt: Which cleaning practice best reduces resuspension of settled particulate matter in an office?

options.text: Use dry dusting with feather dusters every day so that particles are removed more often
Use standard bag vacuums during occupied hours so the cleaning is visible to staff
Use HEPA-filtered vacuuming and damp wiping methods according to a routine schedule
Use leaf blowers in corridors after hours and reoccupy the space the next morning

explanation: HEPA vacuuming and damp wiping capture dust rather than redistributing it into the breathing zone. Cleaning methods and schedules are important parts of maintaining healthy indoor environmental quality.

distractorExplanations.a: Dry dusting lifts settled particles back into the air; damp wiping captures them instead of resuspending them.
distractorExplanations.b: Non-HEPA vacuums exhaust fine particles, and cleaning during occupancy increases occupant exposure to resuspended dust.
distractorExplanations.d: Blowers resuspend dust that later resettles on surfaces occupants touch; they move particles rather than remove them.

prompt: A project is evaluating a basement wellness studio with no operable windows. Which combination best addresses fresh-air quality?

options.text: Rely on transfer air from the adjacent corridor and add portable air cleaners to make up for the lack of operable windows
Install a high-capacity recirculating fan coil with MERV 13 filters, which counts as outdoor-air ventilation
Mechanically provide and verify required outdoor airflow, control pollutant sources and monitor relevant indoor-air conditions
Provide outdoor air at the design rate on paper and measure CO2 once at handover without ongoing monitoring

explanation: Windowless spaces can support good air quality through effective mechanical ventilation, commissioning, source control and monitoring. Plants or water coolers do not replace designed ventilation.

distractorExplanations.a: Transfer air is not outdoor air, and portable cleaners do not supply ventilation; the studio needs verified outdoor airflow.
distractorExplanations.b: Recirculated, filtered air does not dilute CO2 or gaseous contaminants; it does not count as outdoor-air ventilation.
distractorExplanations.d: A design figure plus one handover reading neither verifies delivered airflow nor tracks indoor-air conditions in use.

prompt: Why should a potable-water sampling plan identify both representative outlets and high-risk fixtures?

options.text: It lets the team sample high-risk fixtures alone, since representative outlets just repeat the utility report
It allows the lab to composite samples from many outlets into one result for the whole building
It replaces the need for a water management plan by covering every fixture type once at handover
It helps characterize overall water quality while detecting localized problems

explanation: Water quality can vary across a plumbing system. Sampling a representative set and targeted high-risk locations provides a more useful assessment than testing only one convenient outlet. Localized problems are often caused by specific plumbing materials or low-use conditions.

distractorExplanations.a: Representative outlets show building-wide quality that utility data cannot; dropping them loses the overall picture.
distractorExplanations.b: Compositing dilutes a single bad outlet into an average and hides exactly the localized problems sampling should find.
distractorExplanations.c: A sampling plan is one input to water management; one-time sampling at handover does not replace an ongoing plan.

prompt: A food-service area is considering a self-service salad bar. Which operational control most directly protects food safety?

options.text: Top up the pans with fresh food on top of existing food to reduce waste during long service periods
Rely on sneeze guards at the bar, since they remove the need for cold-holding temperature checks
Maintain required cold-holding temperatures and implement hygiene, cleaning and replenishment procedures
Check food temperatures once at opening and rely on fast turnover for the rest of the service day

explanation: Safe food service depends on temperature control, hygienic handling and routine sanitation. These controls limit pathogen growth and cross-contamination while allowing nutritious foods to be readily available.

distractorExplanations.a: Layering fresh food over older food extends holding time and spreads contamination; pans should be replaced, not topped up.
distractorExplanations.b: Sneeze guards limit contamination from customers but do not control bacterial growth; temperature control is still required.
distractorExplanations.d: A single check cannot show foods stay at safe cold-holding temperatures; monitoring must continue through service.

prompt: Which policy most directly supports breastfeeding employees returning to work?

options.text: Provide a private restroom stall with a chair for expressing milk during scheduled breaks
Offer unpaid leave extensions in place of on-site break time and space for employees who are breastfeeding
Allow milk expression in a shared first-aid room that doubles as a storage area for supplies
Provide reasonable break time and a private, non-toilet lactation space with appropriate amenities

explanation: WELL v2 C09 New Mother Support (Community concept) pairs reasonable break time with a private, hygienic, non-restroom lactation space so employees can express milk safely; the policy complements the physical room design.

distractorExplanations.a: A toilet area is unhygienic for expressing milk; lactation space must be private and not a bathroom.
distractorExplanations.b: Extended leave does not support employees who have returned to work; they need break time and a lactation space.
distractorExplanations.c: A shared first-aid or storage room cannot guarantee the privacy and availability a dedicated lactation space provides.

prompt: A WELL v2 project team is designing open-plan office lighting to support circadian health. Which metric is most directly used to evaluate melanopic (circadian-effective) light exposure?

options.text: Equivalent Melanopic Lux (EML) at the eye
Total lumens per square foot on the workplane
Wattage per fixture regardless of spectrum
Color Rendering Index (CRI) of the lamp

explanation: WELL Light concepts emphasize circadian-effective illumination evaluated at the occupant's eye using melanopic weighting, commonly expressed as EML rather than generic illuminance alone.

distractorExplanations.b: Horizontal workplane lux does not account for vertical eye-level exposure or melanopic spectrum weighting.
distractorExplanations.c: Wattage does not describe spectral content or retinal circadian response.
distractorExplanations.d: CRI describes color rendering quality, not circadian stimulus.

prompt: Which design strategy best supports WELL Movement concepts in a mid-rise office building?

options.text: Locate fire-rated egress stairs at the building core and add signs pointing to them from the lobby
Place attractive, visible stairs near main circulation and reduce reliance on elevators for short trips
Provide a fitness room on the top floor and keep the stairs enclosed behind closed doors for building security
Install faster destination-dispatch elevators so occupants spend less time waiting between floors

explanation: WELL Movement promotes active design by making stairs convenient, visible, and appealing so occupants choose them for everyday vertical travel.

distractorExplanations.a: Enclosed egress stairs at the core are rarely attractive or visible; signs alone do not create an inviting stair.
distractorExplanations.c: A fitness room does not encourage daily stair use, and hidden enclosed stairs push occupants toward elevators.
distractorExplanations.d: Faster elevators make the sedentary option more convenient, which works against Movement goals for short trips.

prompt: Under ASHRAE Standard 55 thermal comfort principles referenced in WELL Thermal Comfort, what does PMV primarily indicate?

options.text: Percentage of occupants predicted to be dissatisfied with the space
Mean radiant temperature of the surfaces surrounding an occupant
Metabolic rate of occupants expressed in met units for each activity
Predicted mean vote of thermal sensation on a comfort scale

explanation: PMV (Predicted Mean Vote) models average thermal sensation based on environmental and personal factors such as air temperature, radiant temperature, humidity, air speed, clothing, and metabolic rate.

distractorExplanations.a: That describes PPD (Predicted Percentage Dissatisfied), which is derived from PMV but is a separate index.
distractorExplanations.b: Mean radiant temperature is one input to the PMV calculation, not what the PMV index itself represents.
distractorExplanations.c: Metabolic rate (met) is an input to PMV alongside clothing, air temperature, radiant temperature, air speed and humidity.

prompt: A project provides sit-stand workstations and interior walking loops. Which WELL concept area do these strategies primarily address?

options.text: Water
Movement
Materials
Sound

explanation: Active furnishings and interior walking paths reduce sedentary behavior and support WELL Movement goals for physical activity in daily building use.

distractorExplanations.a: Water features address hydration and water quality, not physical activity.
distractorExplanations.c: Materials focuses on product ingredient transparency and VOC limits.
distractorExplanations.d: Sound addresses acoustic comfort and noise control.

prompt: Which lighting control approach best reduces circadian disruption from bright artificial light at night in a 24/7 operations center?

options.text: Lower melanopic content and illuminance during night shifts while maintaining task visibility
Raise melanopic content during night shifts to keep workers alert, then dim the lighting at sunrise
Keep a constant 4000 K at full output around the clock so day and night shifts see equal light
Switch to blue-enriched 6500 K lighting overnight but at half the daytime illuminance level

explanation: WELL Light strategies for shift workers include managing spectrum and intensity at night to limit circadian disruption while preserving safe task illumination.

distractorExplanations.b: High melanopic light at night suppresses melatonin and shifts the circadian clock, increasing disruption.
distractorExplanations.c: Constant bright light removes day-night contrast, so night workers still receive circadian-disrupting exposure.
distractorExplanations.d: Halving illuminance does not offset the high melanopic ratio of 6500 K light, which still disrupts circadian rhythm at night.

prompt: A naturally ventilated office in a mild climate allows occupants to open windows. Which thermal comfort framework is often appropriate when occupants have adaptive control?

options.text: PMV/PPD model with fixed clothing and metabolic inputs, as used for sealed air-conditioned offices
Adaptive comfort model with narrower acceptable ranges, since window use makes conditions less stable
Mean radiant temperature limits from the local discomfort section, applied in place of a comfort model
Adaptive comfort model allowing wider acceptable temperature ranges when users can adjust openings

explanation: Adaptive comfort models recognize that acceptable temperature ranges can broaden when occupants can open windows, adjust clothing, or otherwise adapt, as referenced in ASHRAE 55 and WELL Thermal Comfort.

distractorExplanations.a: PMV/PPD suits mechanically conditioned spaces; occupant-controlled naturally ventilated spaces fit the adaptive model.
distractorExplanations.b: The adaptive model allows wider, not narrower, acceptable temperatures because occupants can adapt and control openings.
distractorExplanations.c: Local discomfort limits supplement an overall comfort model; they are not a substitute framework for naturally ventilated spaces.

prompt: Which window treatment strategy best supports both daylight access and glare control for desk workers near perimeter glazing?

options.text: Permanently fritted glazing at 80% coverage, applied uniformly on every facade
Interior blackout roller blinds that occupants lower fully whenever glare appears
Automated or manual shades that block direct sun while preserving diffuse daylight
Dark-tinted glass with 10% visible transmittance on all orientations without shades

explanation: Effective daylight design balances access to natural light with glare control through shading that responds to sun angle, supporting WELL Light visual comfort.

distractorExplanations.a: Dense fixed frit cuts useful daylight on every orientation and cannot respond to changing sun position.
distractorExplanations.b: Fully lowered blackout blinds remove daylight along with glare; the aim is to block direct sun but keep diffuse light.
distractorExplanations.d: Very low visible transmittance sacrifices daylight access and still offers no adjustable control of direct sun.

prompt: A fitness amenity includes on-site exercise space accessible to building occupants. Which WELL domain does this primarily support?

options.text: Community
Nourishment
Air
Movement

explanation: Dedicated exercise facilities encourage regular physical activity, a core WELL Movement strategy beyond incidental stair use or walking.

distractorExplanations.a: Community may overlap socially but the primary intent is physical activity.
distractorExplanations.b: Nourishment addresses healthy food environments, not structured exercise space.
distractorExplanations.c: Air addresses ventilation and pollutant control, not exercise programming.

prompt: What is the primary purpose of measuring vertical illuminance at the eye for daylighting assessments in WELL projects?

options.text: To measure horizontal task illuminance on the desk surface for reading and keyboard work
To calculate annual sunlight exposure (ASE) across the floor plate as an indicator of glare risk
To evaluate light available for visual and circadian effects at the occupant's line of sight
To verify luminaire efficacy in lumens per watt against the allowed lighting power density

explanation: Eye-level vertical illuminance reflects what enters the eye for vision and circadian stimulation, which is more relevant than floor-level metrics alone for WELL Light evaluation.

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses horizontal task illuminance with vertical illuminance at the eye, which determines circadian light exposure.
distractorExplanations.b: ASE is an annual horizontal grid metric for overlit area; it is not a measurement at the occupant's eye.
distractorExplanations.d: Efficacy and lighting power density are energy metrics; they do not describe light reaching the occupant's eye.

prompt: A building operator receives frequent hot-cold complaints in one open office zone despite a central thermostat reading 72°F. What is the best first diagnostic step aligned with thermal comfort management?

options.text: Survey occupants and check local radiant asymmetry, air speed, and solar gains at complaint locations
Recalibrate the central thermostat and raise supply airflow to the whole zone before speaking to occupants
Lower the zone setpoint by two degrees for a week and log whether the number of complaints drops
Move the thermostat into the return-air plenum so it reads the average zone temperature more accurately

explanation: Thermal comfort depends on multiple factors beyond air temperature at one sensor; localized radiant conditions, drafts, and solar load often explain zone complaints under WELL Thermal Comfort principles.

distractorExplanations.b: Zone-wide changes ignore that complaints are local; radiant, air-speed and solar causes must be diagnosed where they occur.
distractorExplanations.c: Changing the setpoint without diagnosis may help hot complaints and worsen cold ones; local conditions need checking first.
distractorExplanations.d: A plenum reading still hides local radiant asymmetry and drafts at desks, which explain mixed hot-cold complaints.

prompt: Which color temperature strategy during daytime hours generally supports alertness in office environments while maintaining visual comfort?

options.text: Warm 2700 K lighting during the day to reduce eye strain and match residential settings
Neutral to cool-white spectrum with adequate melanopic content during working hours
Cool 6500 K lighting at maximum output in the morning and evening, dimmed at midday
Low-intensity lighting below 150 lux with high color rendering for visual comfort

explanation: Daytime lighting with appropriate spectrum and intensity supports visual performance and circadian entrainment; WELL Light encourages designed day-night contrast rather than flat warm dim light all day.

distractorExplanations.a: Warm 2700 K light has low melanopic content, which provides weaker daytime circadian stimulus for alertness.
distractorExplanations.c: Bright cool light in the evening delays the circadian clock; strong melanopic light belongs in daytime working hours.
distractorExplanations.d: Good color rendering does not offset very low illuminance, which gives little melanopic stimulus for daytime alertness.

prompt: A project installs bike storage and showers near the building entrance. Which combination of WELL concepts do these amenities most directly support?

options.text: Thermal Comfort and occupant thermal control options
Community and universal design for site access
Movement and related active transportation support
Water and access to hygiene and handwashing

explanation: Bicycle infrastructure and changing facilities reduce barriers to active commuting, aligning with WELL Movement strategies for physical activity in daily life.

distractorExplanations.a: Showers serve commuters who arrive after active travel; they are not a strategy for controlling indoor temperature.
distractorExplanations.b: Universal design concerns accessibility for people of different abilities, not facilities for cycling commuters.
distractorExplanations.d: Showers here support active commuting under Movement; Water hygiene features address handwashing and water quality.

prompt: Relative humidity in an office is consistently 18% during winter heating. Which occupant impact is most likely?

options.text: Higher risk of mould growth on cold window frames and wall surfaces
Increased dust mite populations in carpets and upholstered seating
Higher perceived warmth leading to more overheating complaints
Dry air discomfort affecting eyes and respiratory mucous membranes

explanation: Very low winter humidity contributes to thermal comfort and health-related dryness complaints; WELL Thermal Comfort considers humidity among environmental comfort factors.

distractorExplanations.a: Mould growth is linked to high humidity and condensation; 18% RH is too dry to support it.
distractorExplanations.b: Dust mites thrive in humid conditions; very low winter humidity suppresses them rather than increasing them.
distractorExplanations.c: Low humidity increases evaporative cooling of the skin, so occupants tend to feel cooler, not warmer.

prompt: Which metric pair is commonly used together to describe thermal environment acceptability under ASHRAE 55?

options.text: PMV and PPD (Predicted Percentage Dissatisfied)
MRT and SHGC (Solar Heat Gain Coefficient)
EML and CCT (Equivalent Melanopic Lux, Color Temperature)
sDA and ASE (Annual Sunlight Exposure)

explanation: PMV estimates mean thermal sensation while PPD estimates the percentage of occupants likely dissatisfied, forming the standard thermal comfort evaluation pair in ASHRAE 55.

distractorExplanations.b: Mean radiant temperature is a PMV input and SHGC is a glazing property; neither pair expresses acceptability under ASHRAE 55.
distractorExplanations.c: EML and CCT are lighting metrics used in WELL Light, not thermal comfort indices from ASHRAE 55.
distractorExplanations.d: sDA and ASE are daylighting metrics from IES LM-83, not ASHRAE 55 thermal acceptability measures.

prompt: A designer locates photocell sensors inside a deep floor plate far from windows. What lighting control issue is most likely?

options.text: Occupancy sensing will switch lights off during meetings because photocells cannot detect motion
Daylight harvesting will dim lights incorrectly because sensors do not see perimeter daylight conditions
Lights will flicker at visible frequencies because photocells change the LED driver output
Circadian tuning will fail because photocells set the colour temperature of each fixture

explanation: Daylight sensors must be placed where they represent the daylight available to the controlled zone; poor sensor location causes inappropriate dimming and energy or comfort problems.

distractorExplanations.a: Photocells sense light levels, not occupancy; occupancy control uses separate motion or presence sensors.
distractorExplanations.c: Flicker depends on driver design; photocell placement affects daylight response, not flicker frequency.
distractorExplanations.d: Photocells used for daylight harvesting control dimming level; tunable spectrum is set by separate controls.

prompt: Which WELL Light strategy helps occupants who receive limited daylight due to interior office locations?

options.text: Provide high-quality electric lighting with appropriate spectrum, intensity, and glare control at workstations
Install tubular daylight devices only in perimeter zones, where occupants already receive window daylight
Raise horizontal desk illuminance to 1,000 lux with warm 2700 K lamps to make up for missing daylight
Provide light-therapy lamps on request while keeping standard overhead lighting with bare lamps in view

explanation: When daylight is unavailable, designed electric lighting can still support visual performance and circadian health through appropriate intensity, spectrum, and control.

distractorExplanations.b: Placing daylight devices at the perimeter helps those who already have windows, not interior occupants lacking daylight.
distractorExplanations.c: More horizontal light from warm lamps adds glare risk and gives weak melanopic stimulus at the eye for interior occupants.
distractorExplanations.d: Ad hoc therapy lamps do not fix base lighting quality, and exposed bare lamps create glare at workstations.

prompt: An office policy encourages walking meetings in interior circulation paths. Which WELL concept does this operational strategy support?

options.text: Materials
Mind
Movement
Sound

explanation: Walking meetings increase daily physical activity during work hours, supporting WELL Movement beyond built infrastructure alone.

distractorExplanations.a: Materials addresses product chemistry and transparency.
distractorExplanations.b: Mind focuses on mental health and cognitive support; walking meetings primarily increase activity.
distractorExplanations.d: Sound addresses acoustic environment quality.

prompt: Which condition most likely causes asymmetric thermal discomfort near a large exterior glass wall on a sunny winter day?

options.text: Radiant temperature difference from solar-heated glazing while air temperature remains moderate
Stratified supply air from overhead diffusers pooling warm air near the ceiling of the perimeter zone
High relative humidity near the glazing raising the perceived air temperature at the desk
Excess outdoor air from the economizer cooling the space below setpoint near the facade

explanation: Radiant asymmetry from warm or cold surfaces is a common thermal comfort issue; occupants may feel hot near sunlit glass even when air temperature seems acceptable.

distractorExplanations.b: Stratification causes vertical temperature differences, not one-sided discomfort facing a sunny glass wall.
distractorExplanations.c: Winter humidity is usually low, and humidity affects whole-body comfort rather than one-sided radiant asymmetry.
distractorExplanations.d: Over-cooling by outdoor air lowers air temperature evenly; the scenario states air temperature remains moderate.

prompt: A project team specifies tunable-white luminaires. What is the primary WELL-related benefit?

options.text: Higher color rendering index than fixed-white LEDs, which is the main circadian lighting metric
Elimination of glare from luminaires, since tunable-white fixtures have lower surface luminance
Reduced flicker at all dimming levels, which WELL treats as the core purpose of tunable fixtures
Ability to adjust spectrum and intensity across the day to support circadian and visual needs

explanation: Tunable-white systems allow programmed or manual shifts in color temperature and output to create day-evening contrast aligned with WELL Light circadian design.

distractorExplanations.a: CRI describes color fidelity; circadian lighting in WELL is measured with melanopic metrics such as EML.
distractorExplanations.b: Tunable spectrum does not reduce luminaire luminance; glare control depends on optics, shielding and placement.
distractorExplanations.c: Flicker performance depends on the driver; tunable-white fixtures exist to vary spectrum and intensity over the day.

prompt: Which personal factor in thermal comfort models accounts for activity level such as seated office work versus walking?

options.text: Community engagement score
Sound transmission class
Filter pressure drop
Metabolic rate (met)

explanation: Metabolic rate describes heat generated by human activity and is a key input in PMV/PPD and adaptive comfort assessments under ASHRAE 55.

distractorExplanations.a: Community engagement is a WELL Community concept, not a thermal model input.
distractorExplanations.b: STC is an acoustic property of assemblies.
distractorExplanations.c: Filter pressure drop relates to HVAC filtration, not occupant metabolism.
